The (overview/quick notes) revised history of the ULR so far as of development (1754-1831)

[spoiler] Mr. L. Lavinworth was born in 1721 to his father Theador and mother Marie, both of whom were Llyndoran nationalists. Theador was an investor and governor, and Marie owned many vineyards, some of which the royal family still owns today. Growing up relatively rich, he went to private schools and eventually university, where he studied public and business administration.  Taking over as the CEO of the Three Seas Lavinsworth company (TSLC) in 1747 with his father still monitoring and advising him, he began to decide on his first big business decision. While deciding on what to do, he became engaged with his university girlfriend Astagna Vilona, marrying her in the spring of 1750. Deciding on pioneering a trade port in an advantageous position, Mr. Lavinsworth eventually gathered a large group of settlers, mercenaries, and tradesmen roughly 160 people all together under the promise of land and an upfront payment equivalent of $10,000 today. He set sail in fall of 1753 despite the birth of his son a year earlier, leaving his wife and son half of his fortune and the company under the control of his father once again for the time of his subsequent adventure.

 He eventually arrived on the northern side of the island of Raira in early 1754. Upon landing on the island and designating a workable area to establish a port, Mr. Lavinsworth designates the area The Settlement of Rorack, named after a friend he made at university. The construction at the settlement would begin as soon as possible, and at a breakneck speed. By the end of three months, the community already consisted of a small port capable of mooring the two ships the colonists sailed across on, two-story houses, two 15 and one 20 men barracks, and 17 homes along with a medical/dining hall (similar size to the 20 man barracks) along with a tailors shop, a lumber yard, and a few fields of crops. By this time the native argos had been spotted near the outskirts, but they were considered either friendly or neutral, gesturing at settlers they could see and leaving the community alone.

By 1757, the port had been expanded and modernized from its crude construction to a more serviceable design, and the establishment of a main road had cemented the settlement as a promising venture. The construction of a small garrison on the outskirts of town provided a base for the new local militia, led by Harry Rainsville who was a veteran of a revolt that failed, fleeing from his home country and eventually finding himself hired by the TSLC. These militia men would be supplied with Mozdam Model-1740 muskets. By this time, there had been multiple sightings of natives, with a few small encounters leaving an estimated five natives and two colonists dead. It would soon be learned that around this time, a war had started between two kingdoms on the island, with the settlement of Rorack being considerably close to the border of the kingdoms.

A small raiding party from the Kingdom of Kaffa beset the settlement, looking to loot the opposing kingdom. They were spotted by hunters while approaching the settlement, giving the militia time to rally and position themselves behind a small stone fence on the south side of the town. The raiding party entered into sight within the hour, and a battle commenced. The militia suffered no casualties, using the power of their muskets and the few mercenaries as higher commanders to repel the party, killing 10 natives. Spurred on by this attack, armed settlers began heading south, marking a period of armed expansion bringing in those looking for money, fame, or land to the Rorack. These settlers would commit various acts, such as burning villages and picking off small war parties when they were found. This period ended around 1761, greatly expanding the land administered by the TSLC from a settlement to roughly 10% of the island.

With expansion came prosperity, and this spurred Sir Lavinsworth to sponsor his own private army, the Rorack Jungle Rifles. These men would use brutal tactics along with small horse-drawn cannons to go on what would evolve into a 14 year long campaign, expanding the land owned by the TSLC massively with only the mountains proving a large difficulty in the subduing of the natives there. This devastated native nations and culture, leaving many natives displaced with settlers moving in soon after to build on the land, often shooting any native on sight. This yet again further brought more people to the island, and a nation began forming under the command of Sir Lavinsworth. With a thriving economy from port activity, opportunity for resources and land drew other wealthy individuals to the TSLC, investing in it and sometimes even moving out to Rorack themselves so they could see the progress in front of them.

By the year of 1775, Sir Lavinsworth managed to accumulate enough people he trusted to be knowledgeable and trustworthy to found the Kingdom of Lavia. He decided on halfway between a constitutional monarchy and an absolute, allowing a consul to be elected by the people and advise him on what to do, and were also allowed to pass laws pertaining to the economy, public services, and in general laws pertaining to local/national impacts. The king however had final decisions on military and diplomatic matters with a sizable amount of voting power in the consul if he saw a law as unreasonable. Sir Lavinsworths first decree was to colonize/invade the three large islands to the south of the nearby Westmore due to the discovery of iron on the islands, which the nation lacked and had to import at the time. 

Although the invasion of the Manzarno, Makinar, Rasami islands was the first military campaign of the new monarchy (1777), it was mostly similar to the TSLC takeover of Raiara except for the actions of King Vienalo of the Rasami Kingdom. King Vienalo was a particularly well connected individual, mostly due to his nation being in a valuable trade route and actions taken by himself to be particularly more informed than other leaders in the area. After discovering about the brutal colonization of Manzanaro island, he figured the foreign army would continue south and take both the island of Makinar and Rasami. With this information, he sailed with a royal procession to Manzanaro island, and attempted to negotiate with the incoming force. Being successful in his endeavors, the negotiation promised him and his Kingdom a relative level of freedom and self-governance as well as the election of their own representative to the consul. 

This campaign ended sometime in 1786, with smaller campaigns still going on to secure the Yumar island chain and the multiple islands around Raira, including Primank. This island was particularly north of Rorack, creating a strategic chokepoint. Sir Lavinsworth deemed this particularly important and sent army engineers and troops not deployed to construct a garrison, fort, and small port. About this time also, West Shamati traders began sailing to the northern part of Raira, trading things such as multicolored linen blankets with Lavian soldiers. This eventually opened up diplomacy with the Kingdom of Swabati, expanding trade and cementing the Kingdom of Lavia as a nation. Sir Lavinsworth and King Kavavenga became very good friends during talks of trade and the Ketu friendship treaty, leading to Lavian influence somewhat contributing to the Swabati kingdom staying free from interference from Elseyr and Vespuria.

With his ideas of colonial expansion satiated and the industrial revolution underway, Sir Lavinsworth turned his focus to the southern islands and their abundance of iron. The need for metals was still handled completely by import, so opening mines was the first step to economic independence for the Kingdom of Lavia. The import of mechanical components and engineers to help establish factories and mines both on the southern islands and Raira, taking advantage of the abundance of gold as well as copper. The crude oil on the island would be tapped a little during this time, however only being used for lanterns as an alternative to whale oil. Along with the fast industrialization, companies viewed it as an easy market leading to many companies opening factories in the kingdom and the beginnings of national weapons production. A weapon manufacturer from Elseyr who opened up multiple factories during this time was contracted to make various different items for the Lavian military and train the first of the royal armorers, who would go onto found the Royal Lavian Arms Company (RLAC, mostly called R-LAC (pronounced R-Lack.)) One model of rifle ordered by the Lavian Royal Army (LRA) was specifically the Magenson Rifle, one of the first breech loading rifles to be purchased by a military with the large benefit of being able to load while prone. However due to the high cost of these rifles, they were only given to the RJR, which had evolved into an elite unit rather than being the entire army as it had been in the era of the TSLC. 

At the age of 68 in 1789, Sir Lavinsworth decided to step down from the throne due to him deciding his mental state was declining and affecting his ability to rule. In a ceremony where the Raria Crown (A crown similar to a laurel crown in design) was first revealed, Sir Lavinsworth Gave the crown to his son William, making him the second king of the Kingdom of Lavia at the age of 36. This crowning also had another influence due to unrest on the island of Rasami and William having married the daughter of King Vienalo, it is suspected that the crowning happened to placate the people of Rasami by putting one of their royalty in a high position in government. If intended or not, it did lower the unrest in Rasami. Perhaps due to his wifes influence and the study of other such nations, William proclaimed Greater Lavia (think Great Britain), turning Rasami into a state of the kingdom instead of an occupied territory. This gave much more freedom to the people of Rasami, such as the ability to vote for their consul representatives and also changing the presence of the Lavian Royal Army into one of protecting instead of being an occupying force. William was neither very progressive nor conservative, but his wife influenced him to pass the Argos Peoples Bill, giving Argos natives equal rights to those of the Vespurians who immigrated and settled in Raria. This bill however only applied to those in areas that were states.

Throughout the 1790s to 1822, Greater Lavia experienced a time of relative peace and prosperity. The industrial revolution spurred the demand for now widely available goods made accessible by factories, leading to much more international trade and benefiting Lavia due to its location near vital trade routes and factories were quickly constructed in the southern islands to satiate demand and expand the economy. The southern islands experienced the most industrialization due to the ready access to iron, contributing to the integration of the southern islands as a state due to them being a staple of the economy. The kingdom established Primark island as its main military base in 1809, using the industrialization and expanded mining of iron in the southern islands to construct a large naval and army base (named Seger Military Base) meant to also be a ship construction yard, army training ground, and also the first RLAC factory, producing rifles and cannon barrels. RLAC expanded to produce cannon rounds and the gunpowder to make them, establishing a fully civil production base for the military. The RLAC would take time to be able to supply the entirety of the army though, so many chapter items such as gunpowder and small items were still mostly imported for some time. The Lavian navy also was kickstarted by this project, with the establishment of the Seger Naval Design Institute when the dockyards and drydock of the base were finished in 1812, however the bain body of Lavian ship production would stay in the southern islands due to ease of supply and ready worker base already there, leaving the SNDI to evolve to experiment and test ever evolving ship designs. The construction of Seger military base would finish in 1829, interupted by the Swabati-Wituli war. 

As Lavia was developing and industrializing, West Shamat was impacted heavily by the industrial revolution. The new availability of weapons and increased trade allowed Shamati kingdoms to war with newfound efficiency and bloodshed. Historically, the Witulo and Swabati kingdoms were relatively peaceful, with few wars between each other compared to other nations in Shamat at the time with the exception of a war in 1779 that resulted in the loss of some mainland Shamat territory, giving the Swabati kingdom mainland territory which it had lacked since the 1650s. The Wituli kingdom had been more aggressive to its neighbors, and the mainland territory of the Swabatis was on the list of conquests.This led to a three year long war between 1821 and 1824, with Swabati and Lavian forces holding a short defensive line and then advancing into Watuli territory. Hardened from years of colonial expansion with a large amount of help from Swabati scouts, the advance went well, until reaching the capital city of the enemy empire. This city was particularly tough to take, not only due to the ferocity of the fighting, but due to the devastation the Lavian fleet did to the city, turning the battle into a form of trench combat with destroyed buildings acting as the trenches and any path or road acting as no man's land. The war ended with the Swabati kingdom taking most of the coastal territory of the Wituli kingdom. Shortly after the peace, the Wituli royals were killed and the remnants of the empire crumbled into infighting and small city-states.

Following the war, The aging King William stepped down at the age of 73 in 1826, handing the crown to his son, Michael, aged 51. Michael would however pass away soon after at the age of 56 from what would later be confirmed as liver cancer, leaving Lavia to his son Fredrick (aged 26) in 1831.  [/spoiler]
